_comment: ADVISORY-ONLY detection HINTS for suspicious install/build-time script behavior in supply-chain manifests (setup.py, pyproject build hooks, package.json pre/postinstall, etc.). These are heuristics for HUMAN review, NOT exploits and NOT confirmed malice. Severity is INFO or LOW ONLY and must NEVER be graded HIGH/CRITICAL. Many legitimate packages match these patterns; treat every hit as 'worth a look', not 'compromised'. Each pattern: name, regex (Python re, case-insensitive intended), severity, note.

patterns.name: curl-piped-to-shell
patterns.note: Install/build step downloads a script and pipes it straight to a shell. Common in installers but unverifiable code execution; review the URL and pin a hash.

patterns.name: wget-piped-to-shell
patterns.note: wget output piped to a shell at install/build time. Same risk profile as curl|bash.

patterns.name: base64-decode-then-exec
patterns.note: Base64-decoded payload passed to exec(). A frequent obfuscation pattern in malicious packages; confirm what the blob decodes to.

patterns.name: base64-decode-then-eval
patterns.note: Base64-decoded content passed to eval(). Obfuscated dynamic execution; review the decoded source.

patterns.name: eval-of-network-content
patterns.note: eval() applied directly to downloaded content. Remote code execution by design; should be inspected.

patterns.name: exec-of-network-content
patterns.note: exec() applied to downloaded content. Executes remote code at install/build time; review the source URL.

patterns.name: os-system-in-setup
patterns.note: os.system() call present. Build scripts sometimes need shell-outs; flagged for review of what command is run.

patterns.name: subprocess-shell-true
patterns.note: subprocess invoked with shell=True. Shell injection surface if any argument is attacker-influenced; review the command construction.

patterns.name: subprocess-in-setup
patterns.note: subprocess imported in a packaging/build script. Common and often legitimate; included so a reviewer can confirm intent.

patterns.name: request-to-raw-ip
patterns.note: Hard-coded raw IPv4 URL (not a domain). Legitimate packages almost always use named hosts; raw IPs in install/build code warrant a look.

patterns.name: outbound-request-in-setup
patterns.note: Outbound HTTP request inside packaging/build code. Could be legitimate (fetch data file) or exfil/staging; verify the endpoint.

patterns.name: socket-connect-in-setup
patterns.note: Raw socket connection in build/install code. Unusual for legitimate packaging; inspect the destination.

patterns.name: env-var-harvest
patterns.note: Environment variables read and then sent over the network near install time. Classic secret/token exfiltration shape; review carefully.

patterns.name: marshal-or-pickle-loads
patterns.note: marshal/pickle deserialization in build code. Deserializing untrusted bytes is code execution; confirm the source is trusted/local.

patterns.name: compile-then-exec
patterns.note: Source compiled then exec()'d. Dynamic execution that can hide intent; review the compiled string's origin.

patterns.name: getattr-builtins-dynamic
patterns.note: Dynamic lookup against __builtins__. Common obfuscation to reach exec/eval indirectly; inspect what attribute is fetched.

patterns.name: chmod-exec-bit
patterns.note: Sets an executable bit during install/build. Often legitimate for bundled binaries; flagged so a reviewer can confirm the file.

patterns.name: write-to-autostart-or-cron
patterns.note: Install/build code touches a persistence/autostart location. Legitimate packages rarely do this; treat as a strong review hint.

patterns.name: tempfile-then-execute
patterns.note: Writes to a temp path then executes it. Common dropper pattern; confirm the temp file content is benign.

patterns.name: powershell-invocation
patterns.note: Encoded/hidden PowerShell invoked from install/build code. Strong obfuscation/persistence indicator; review the command.

patterns.name: npm-preinstall-shell
patterns.note: package.json preinstall runs shell/inline-code. preinstall executes before dependency review; verify the command.

patterns.name: npm-postinstall-shell
patterns.note: package.json postinstall runs shell/inline-code. postinstall is the most-abused npm lifecycle hook; inspect the command.

patterns.name: npm-install-script-shell
patterns.note: package.json install lifecycle runs shell/download. Review what the install hook fetches and runs.

patterns.name: npm-node-dash-e-inline
patterns.note: npm lifecycle hook executes inline Node code (node -e). Inline code in a hook can hide behavior; read the snippet.

patterns.name: npm-lifecycle-base64
patterns.note: npm lifecycle hook decodes base64. Obfuscated install-time payload; decode and inspect.

patterns.name: npm-lifecycle-env-exfil
patterns.note: npm lifecycle hook reads env vars and contacts the network. Token/secret exfiltration shape; review the endpoint.

patterns.name: child-process-in-package
patterns.note: Node child_process required (in a script field or bundled install helper). Often legitimate build tooling; flagged for review.

patterns.name: dynamic-import-from-url
patterns.note: Module name/source derived from a network value before import. Remote-controlled imports; verify the resolution path.

patterns.name: hardcoded-credential-like-token
patterns.note: Credential-shaped literal in build/install code. May be a placeholder or a real leaked secret; confirm it is not live.

patterns.name: atexit-or-import-time-side-effect
patterns.note: Side-effecting action registered for interpreter exit during install/build. Unusual placement; review what runs at exit.
